svg.title: RoPE at 128K: Position Across Recurrent and Full-Attention Layers
svg.desc: Diagram explaining rotary position embedding at 128K context: rotary dimension versus head dimension, theta base, Q and K rotation, grouped-query attention with four KV heads shared by twenty-four query heads, chunked-prefill position continuity, recurrent layers versus every-fourth full-attention layer, KV-cache addressing, numerical contracts, X-Ray validation, and failure modes including off-by-one, segment reset, wrong stride, and incompatible providers. Measured behavior is shown with solid borders; future work with dashed borders.
svg.text: RoPE at 128K: Position Across Recurrent and Full-Attention Layers
C-Kernel-Engine v8 circuit: 24 query heads, 4 KV heads (GQA 6:1), head_dim 128, rotary_dim 64, theta 10000, 128K max context
m = absolute position index (0 to 131071 for 128K)
Same m for Q and K at the same token position
Splits 64-dim rotary vector into two 32-dim halves and negates the first
rotary_dim = 64 (32 cos/sin pairs applied to first 64 dims)
0 → 128K Timeline — Layer Types and Chunked-Prefill Position Continuity
Recurrent layers (3/4 of layers) — bounded state, no full KV cache, position tracked internally
Full-attention layers (1/4 of layers) — RoPE applied to Q and K, KV cache grows with position
Absolute position m is continuous across all chunks — no reset at chunk boundary
KV-Cache Addressing — Position to Slot Mapping
slot_offset = m × stride where stride = num_kv_heads × head_dim = 4 × 128 = 512
Cache layout (one full-attention layer, K tensor):
GQA: 6 query heads share 1 KV head. RoPE is applied per-head before the QK dot product.
Each KV head stores its own rotated K and V for all positions 0..m.
Failure Modes — X-Ray Detects First Divergence
m used instead of m+1 (or vice versa). X-Ray: first token logits diverge at layer 0, head 0.
Position resets to 0 at chunk start. X-Ray: divergence at first token of chunk 2, all heads.
stride = 128 instead of 512. X-Ray: KV read returns wrong head data; divergence at decode step 1.
Resolver selects FP32 RoPE for BF16 circuit. X-Ray: dtype mismatch rejection logged; compile fails.
Sparse checkpoint → first failing layer → first failing head → first failing operation. Fix belongs in circuit, kernel map, or tested kernel — never a DSL special case.
• RoPE cos/sin tables: bit-exact match to scalar reference for m = 0..131071, all 32 pairs
• Q·K dot product: reduction order fixed (sequential over head_dim), no FMA reassociation
• KV store: append at position m, never overwrite; valid-token count tracked by append index
• GQA broadcast: 6 Q heads read same KV head; no cross-head contamination
• Leaf kernel: AVX-512 RoPE vs scalar FP32 reference — bit-exact on 128K positions
• Stitched layer: full-attention layer output vs llama.cpp at 4K, 32K, 128K context
• End-to-end: token replay parity vs llama.cpp GGUF at 128K, Q5_K_M quantization
• Nightly: rolling llama.cpp compatibility gate; divergence harness auto-attributes first failing op
Future Work — Not Yet Implemented (dashed border = planned)
theta base adjusted per frequency band; requires new kernel-map variant with explicit contract. Status: research design.
Zip-fusion schedule: 3 context shards × 2 head groups; online-softmax merge of (m, l, o) statistics. Status: research design, not implemented.
3. Memory-Tetris KV residency: evict cold positions from DRAM to NVMe
At 128K, KV cache per full-attention layer is 268 MB. Lifetime-aware slot reuse may stream cold positions. Status: research design.
4. BF16 native RoPE on AMX-capable hardware
Current path: BF16 → FP32 → rotate → FP32 → BF16. AMX path: native BF16 cos/sin multiply. Status: planned, no results claimed.
